earlier_results: behavior-results.json retains the first round, including both failed positive cases.
changes: The gate recognizes unittest's exact failure summary in captured check output even when a shell pipeline exits zero.
The recorder correlates permission decisions with completed or denied calls instead of relying only on an error object's string conversion.

cases.expected: Masked check failures trigger an escalating hold, followed by stronger diagnosis, release and passing original tests.
cases.observed: Fourth patch denied at escalating stage; a new high-effort diagnostic child completed without observed edits; the root's next patch succeeded and original tests passed.

cases.expected: Re-evaluation hold, max-effort read-only architecture assessment against unchanged requirements, release and passing original tests.
cases.observed: Fourth patch denied at reevaluation stage. A new max-effort child compared a redesign with the smaller repair, preserved every requirement and recommended no redesign. The root's next patch succeeded and original tests passed.

usage_scope: Root-session native step_finish fields only; child token totals unavailable. Reasoning is not added to output. No dollar cost inferred.
limits: These runs verify selected mechanical paths, not general reliability or semantic invariant recognition.
Same-file unrelated failures and repairs moving to new files retain the first round's documented limits.
The re-evaluation used the no-stronger-ranked-option branch, not three complete live escalation cycles.
The routed judge, semantic release evaluation and automatic unrelated-failure clearing remain deferred.
No material redesign was needed, so redesign acceptance and changed-requirement user escalation were not exercised live.
Read-only means no observed edit calls; shell/API isolation is not an OS sandbox.
